pageCoverage.notes: Cover identifies Lecture 53 Electrical Actuators; institutional attribution and no technical problem.
Learning objective only: understand electrical actuators used in robots.
Agenda lists electromagnetic principles, electric/DC/AC motors, DC control and stepper motors.

Force per unit length explicitly defined below F=I cross B. Right-hand diagram is conventional-current cross field. Body translation wording is unnecessarily restrictive; current can exist in a stationary wire.

F=BIL shown for perpendicular length L; conductor motion induces EMF only with geometric flux/motional conditions. Broad DC-prevalence statement is contextual. Position/speed control applications listed.

Faraday e=-dphi/dt and flux-change explanation; word charge is a typographical mistake for change. Coil turns and flux linkage need declared conventions. Opposes change, not universally the existing flux.
Opposite active-side forces create a couple. Current reverses through the coil after a half turn to maintain torque sense; diagram is illustrative, not a calibrated angle graph.
Four field poles surround central armature conductors. Rotating segmented commutator contacted by brushes; reverse either field or armature current, not both, to reverse torque.

Constant PM field; effective N conductor convention; T=NBILb=Kt I and Kv speed back EMF. Opposite forces separated by b make a couple Fb. Kv here means back-EMF coefficient, not rpm-per-volt speed constant.

Series armature R,L and back EMF circuit; displayed algebra explicitly neglects L. Torque line intercepts rise with V, slope fixed. Ideal no-load torque zero ignores internal loss. Inductive current cannot jump in an actual voltage step.

Series field and armature share current; simultaneous polarity reversal preserves torque. High starting torque/high no-load speed. Printed current-versus-torque curve is qualitatively convex despite unsaturated I proportional sqrt(T), so not a quantitative law.

Prose says field/armature parallel, but sketch puts Ra/La in a shared path before the split. Good speed regulation is qualified; fixed-field current/torque should be linear rather than the drawn curve. Proper shunt topology needs field across supply and separate full armature branch.

Compound prose highest starting torque conflicts with Average table entry. Table says shunt high resistance/good speed/average start; series low/poor/high; compound shunt high plus series low/average/average. Drawing displays two parallel-looking field branches rather than clear series-plus-shunt wiring. Preserve conflict.

pageCoverage.notes: PM cutaway explicitly labels brush and commutator, encoder, magnet, ironless winding, reduction gearhead and output shaft. Permanent magnets avoid field excitation loss but do not remove armature or friction losses.

PWM varies mean armature voltage from a fixed supply. PM current directly sets torque; speed additionally depends on voltage, back EMF and load. Duty changes average voltage; frequency alone at fixed duty does not.

H-bridge S1/S4 versus S2/S3 diagonals drive opposite polarities. Same-side S1/S3 would short the rails. Lower transistor/diode diagram illustrates A/B commands and inductive recirculation, not universal logic levels for every topology.

Tachogenerator analogue feedback goes through ADC; encoder branch uses digital code conversion. Both pictured forward paths retain DAC and analogue amplifier. No controller transfer function or stability parameters supplied.

BLDC switched stator coils and PM rotor eliminate brushed mechanical commutation. Source describes three-sensor sequencing, not a universal ban on sensorless estimation; PM and coils exert equal/opposite interaction.

AC classification single/polyphase each branches into induction/synchronous. Frequency influences speed with pole count and induction slip qualification. Cheaper/difficult-speed-control statements lack universal scope.
Induction machine transformer analogy: stationary primary, freely rotating secondary and magnetic air gap. The all-AC-rotors-induction phrase overgeneralizes beyond induction machines.

Squirrel cage copper/aluminium bars and end rings close rotor currents with no external connection. Single ideal main winding at rest produces no preferred starting torque; auxiliary arrangements required.

Illustrated PM synchronous rotor locks to rotating field. One pole pair yields one revolution per supply cycle; more pairs reduce mechanical speed. Blanket not-self-starting claim needs fixed-frequency versus controlled-drive qualification; not all synchronous rotors must be PM.

Stepper pulse count/rate control nominal displacement/speed if steps are followed. Listed counts12,24,72,144,180,200 give30,15,5,2.5,2,1.8 degrees. PM rotor N/S; W1 left/right, W2 top/bottom. PM/VR classification not exhaustive of hybrid designs.

VR ferromagnetic toothed rotor seeks minimum reluctance/max flux. Eight paired stator poles A/B/C/D surround six rotor teeth; adjacent ideal axes45 versus teeth60 gives15 degree nearest alignment step. Phase means independent stator winding. Holding torque is energized stationary resistance to displacement, not the confusing reversing-spindle clause.

Selection factors speed range, torque-speed, reversibility, duty cycle, starting torque and power. Separate driver peak, continuous motor boundary and commutation limit plotted; no guarantee of safe continuous operation from peak curve alone. Need enlarged graph for precise qualitative target reading.
Operating point is equal motor/load torque at same speed. Declining motor and increasing load curves yield stabilizing local imbalance; generic intersection alone need not be stable.
Below depicted equilibrium motor torque exceeds load and accelerates; above it load exceeds motor and slows. Voltage changes motor curve and equilibrium speed.

Summary adds coreless construction, DC/AC applications, servo motor+encoder+closed position loop, possible not universal .01degree accuracy, stepper open-loop basics and microstepping. Application lists are examples not exclusive technology capabilities.
Four book references only; no additional equation or executable code.
Thank-you slide only.
